title: Split idempotents orthogonal on a module force independent families and a cardinality bound
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $D$ be a unital $K$-algebra, and let $Q$ be a unital left $D$-module with the induced $K$-vector-space structure. Let $I$ be any set, and let $u_i,r_i\in D$ for $i\in I$ satisfy $r_iu_i=1_D$. Put $p_i=u_ir_i$ and suppose that for distinct $i,j$ the product $p_ip_j$ acts as zero on $Q$: $(p_ip_j)x=0$ for every $x\in Q$. For every $0\ne q\in Q$, the family $(u_iq)_{i\in I}$ is $K$-linearly independent, meaning that every finite relation $\sum_{i\in F}t_i u_iq=0$ has $t_i=0$ for all $i\in F$. Moreover, for every spanning set $W\subseteq Q$ (every vector is a finite $K$-linear combination of elements of $W$), there is an injection $I\to W$ whenever $Q\ne0$. In particular, if $I$ is uncountable and $Q$ has a countable spanning set [def-sfb-countable-set], then $Q=0$. No topology on $Q$, faithfulness of the $D$-action, or equality $p_ip_j=0$ inside $D$ is assumed.

proof.text: Consider a finite relation $\sum_{i\in F}t_ix_i=0$ and fix $k\in F$. Action by a fixed element of $D$ is $K$-linear, since scalars from $K$ are central in the $K$-algebra $D$ and the $K$-action on $Q$ is induced. Applying $p_k$ to the relation and using step 1 gives $t_kx_k=0$. Applying $r_k$ gives $t_kq=0$. If $t_k\ne0$, multiplication by its inverse in the field [def-weil-field] would give $q=0$, a contradiction. Thus every $t_k=0$, which proves precisely the stated finite-relation form of linear independence.

proof.text: Now suppose $I$ is uncountable and a countable set $W$ spans $Q$. If $Q\ne0$, step 3 gives an injection $f:I\to W$. By [def-sfb-countable-set], countability of $W$ gives an injection $g:W\to\mathbf N$. The composite $g\circ f$ is injective: equality of its values first implies equality of the $f$-values, then equality of their indices. This contradicts uncountability of $I$ in the same definition. Hence $Q=0$.
